summary: Claude Code invoked hyperpowers:brainstorming, explicitly classified the "move API config into a settings module" brief as ARCHITECTURAL, ran a question/approach flow, wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-settings-module-design.md, presented it for review with no code touched, and only proceeded (to writing-plans) after I said "looks good, go ahead".
reasoning: Every acceptance criterion is supported by direct evidence from the session JSONL log and the workdir filesystem: brainstorming skill loaded first, explicit architectural classification, spec file written under docs/hyperpowers/specs/, spec surfaced for human approval with zero production-code changes (git status clean apart from .gitignore), and implementation planning started only after I approved. Neither bounded-skip nor spike paths were taken.

observations.description: Codex spec-review gate did not produce a verdict: agent reported "The Codex review did not complete — that is not an approval. Preflight reported ok, but the installed companion is a stub (codexVersion 0.0.0-stub): both round-1 lenses exited 0 with an empty {} payload, and status --json shows no job records at all." The agent handled it gracefully and logged an ungated-ledger event 20260917T094552Z-87355-8970, but the stub plugin produced no independent review.

The agent created a .gitignore containing docs/superpowers and docs/hyperpowers, so the spec document it wrote is deliberately untracked/uncommitted. If graders expect a 'committed spec file', this ignore behavior could be surprising.

The brainstorming Q&A ran 6 sequential questions (env source, module shape, config shape, environments, tooling, test seam) plus an approval question. Thorough, but one question per turn with multi-tab checkbox/Submit widgets is fairly heavy keyboard navigation (Right arrow to reach Submit tab was non-obvious).

The agent unilaterally 'skipped the Codex approach gate' with an explanation; it offered to reopen the config.json alternative, but the skipped-gate announcement may look like ceremony bypass to a reviewer skimming.

criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use list begins with `Skill: hyperpowers:brainstorming`; `grep -o '"skill":"[^"]*"' ... | uniq -c` returned `1 "skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"` and `1 "skill":"hyperpowers:writing-plans"` (the latter only after approval).

criteria.criterion: Classified ARCHITECTURAL and wrote spec doc to docs/.../specs/ before presenting design
criteria.evidence: Assistant text in log: "**Classification: architectural.** The first edit is one line in `app.js`, but the request names structure this repo doesn't have ... so this gets the full path: questions → approaches → design → spec." File exists: coding-agent-workdir/docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-settings-module-design.md (`# Settings Module Design ... Status: Approved design, pending implementation plan`).

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before any implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-settings-module-design.md ... Please review it and tell me if you want changes. Once you approve, the next step is the writing-plans skill ... I won't touch code before then." `git status --short` in the workdir showed only `?? .gitignore` — no edits to app.js/index.html, no settings.js.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify bounded / skip spec
criteria.evidence: Explicit "Classification: architectural" quote above; the only in-chat design was followed by an actual spec file on disk. grep for 'bounded' in assistant text returned no self-classification as bounded.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify spike / throwaway probe
criteria.evidence: grep -i 'spike' over assistant-authored text in the session log returned no matches (only 'architectural' and 'bounded' hits from the skill document text); no probe plan was presented.
